items.stem: What shape is the graph of y = x² − 4x + 1?
options: An ∩-shaped parabola with a maximum point
A U-shaped parabola with a minimum point
items.answer: A U-shaped parabola with a minimum point
items.markingKey: The coefficient of x² is positive, so the parabola opens upwards.

items.stem: Explain why the graph of y = 4 − x² has a maximum point.
items.answer: The coefficient of x² is negative, so y decreases as x moves away from 0 in either direction; the greatest value is 4 at x = 0.
items.markingKey: B1 negative x² coefficient; B1 maximum (0, 4) [2]

items.stem: Explain how the line of symmetry of a quadratic graph can be found from its two roots.
items.answer: The parabola is symmetrical, so the line of symmetry is halfway between the roots: x = (p + q)/2.
items.markingKey: B1 symmetry; B1 midpoint of roots [2]

items.stem: What are the asymptotes of y = 1/x?

items.stem: Explain why the graph of y = 5/x has no point where x = 0.
items.answer: Division by zero is undefined, so there is no value of y when x = 0; the y-axis is an asymptote.
items.markingKey: B1 division by zero; B1 asymptote [2]

items.stem: Explain why the graph of y = 3ˣ never goes below the x-axis.
items.answer: A positive number raised to any power is positive, so y is always greater than 0.

Describe the difference between the shapes of y = x³ and y = −x³.
items.answer: y = x³ rises from bottom left to top right; y = −x³ is its reflection in the x-axis, falling from top left to bottom right. Both pass through the origin.
items.markingKey: B1 each shape described; B1 reflection [2]

items.stem: Explain why exponential growth eventually overtakes any quadratic growth such as y = x².
items.answer: An exponential is multiplied by a constant factor for each step in x, so it increases ever faster; for large x, 2ˣ is far larger than x².
items.markingKey: B1 constant multiplying factor; B1 comparison for large x [2]

items.stem: Explain why a stationary point is not always a maximum or minimum.
items.answer: The gradient can be zero without changing sign (e.g. y = x³ at the origin), giving a stationary point of inflection.

items.markingKey: (a) B1 B1 B1 (one per term) [3] (b) M1 x = 0 in tangent equation; A1 [2]

items.stem: Kwame finds the stationary point of y = x² + 2x + 1 at x = −1. Since d²y/dx² = 2, which is positive, Kwame says it is a maximum. Explain whether Kwame is correct.
items.answer: Not correct: a positive second derivative means the gradient is increasing, so the point is a minimum (the parabola is U-shaped).
items.markingKey: B1 positive second derivative ⇒ minimum; B1 reason [2]

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the stationary point on y = 2x² − 12x − 2 and state whether it is a maximum or a minimum.
items.markingKey: M1 dy/dx = 4x − 12 = 0; A1 x = 3; A1 y = −20; B1 nature (a > 0).

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the stationary points on the curve y = x³ − 3x² − 24x − 1 and determine their nature.
items.markingKey: B1 dy/dx = 3x² − 6x − 24; M1 = 0, factorise 3(x + 2)(x − 4) → x = −2, 4; A1 y-values; M1 d²y/dx² = 6x − 6; A1 natures.
